q-89652.name: Question 1
q-89652.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{{x}^{7}},\, & x\ge 1 \\ 0,\, & x<1\end{aligned}
$$

its cumulative distribution function is 

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<1 \\ h(x),\, & x\ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the function $h(x).$
q-89652.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $x\ge 1,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1 \\ {\int }_{1}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t, & x\ge 1\end{aligned}
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{1}^{x}\frac{6}{{t}^{7}}\,\text{d}t \\ \text{ } & ={-\frac{1}{{t}^{6}}|}_{1}^{x} \\  & =-\frac{1}{{x}^{6}}+1 \\  & =1-\frac{1}{{x}^{6}}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1 \\ 1-\frac{1}{{x}^{6}}, & x\ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$

q-89564.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{1-x},\, & x\ge 1 \\ 0,\, & x<1\end{aligned}
$$

its cumulative distribution function is 

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<1 \\ h(x),\, & x\ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1 \\ {\int }_{1}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t, & x\ge 1\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{1}^{x}{e}^{1-t}\,\text{d}t \\ \text{ } & =-{e}^{1-t}{|}_{1}^{x} \\  & =-{e}^{1-x}+1 \\  & =1-{e}^{1-x}.\end{aligned}

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1, \\ 1-{e}^{1-x}, & x\ge 1.\end{aligned}

q-210765.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\frac{{e}^{-|x/4|}}{8},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ),
$$

its cumulative distribution function is

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}h(x),\, & x<0 \\ 1-\frac{{e}^{-x/4}}{2},\, & x\ge 0\end{aligned}
$$

where $h(x)=${{field-1}}.
q-210765.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that involves an absolute value, the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}\frac{{e}^{t/4}}{8}\,\text{d}t, & x<0 \\ {\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{{e}^{t/4}}{8}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{{e}^{-t/4}}{8}\,\text{d}t, & x\ge 0\end{aligned}
$$

Let's compute the integrals.

- If $x\le 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}\frac{{e}^{t/4}}{8}\,\text{d}t & ={\frac{{e}^{t/4}}{2}|}_{-\infty }^{x} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x/4}}{2},\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{{e}^{t/4}}{8}\,\text{d}t & ={\frac{{e}^{x/4}}{2}|}_{x=0} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- If $x>0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{{e}^{-t/4}}{8}\,\text{d}t & =-{\frac{{e}^{-t/4}}{2}|}_{0}^{x} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-x/4}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{{e}^{-t/4}}{8}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{{e}^{-t/4}}{8}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{1}{2}+(-\frac{{e}^{-x/4}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =1-\frac{{e}^{-x/4}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{e}^{x/4}}{2}, & x<0 \\ 1-\frac{{e}^{-x/4}}{2}, & x\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\frac{6{e}^{3x}}{\pi (1+{e}^{6x})},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ),
$$

find the cumulative distribution function $F(x).$
q-126212.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a continuous random variable $X$ is the function $F(x)$ defined by

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}\frac{6{e}^{3t}}{\pi (1+{e}^{6t})}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\frac{2\operatorname{arctan}⁡{e}^{3t}}{\pi }|}_{-\infty }^{x} \\  & =\frac{2\operatorname{arctan}⁡{e}^{3x}}{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

q-210762.name: Question 8
q-210762.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=2{e}^{-|4x|},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ),
$$

its cumulative distribution function is

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{e}^{4x}}{2},\, & x\le 0 \\ h(x),\, & x>0\end{aligned}
$$

where $h(x)=${{field-1}}.
q-210762.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that involves an absolute value, the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}2{e}^{4t}\,\text{d}t, & x\le 0 \\ {\int }_{-\infty }^{0}2{e}^{4t}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{x}2{e}^{-4t}\,\text{d}t, & x>0\end{aligned}
$$

Let's compute the integrals. 

- If $x\le 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}2{e}^{4t}\,\text{d}t & ={\frac{{e}^{4t}}{2}|}_{-\infty }^{x} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{4x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In particular, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}2{e}^{4t}\,\text{d}t & ={\frac{{e}^{4x}}{2}|}_{x=0} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- If $x>0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{x}2{e}^{-4t}\,\text{d}t & =-{\frac{{e}^{-4t}}{2}|}_{0}^{x} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-4x}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}2{e}^{4t}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{x}2{e}^{-4t}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{1}{2}+(-\frac{{e}^{-4x}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =1-\frac{{e}^{-4x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{e}^{4x}}{2},\, & x\le 0, \\ 1-\frac{{e}^{-4x}}{2},\, & x>0.\end{aligned}
$$

q-89634.name: Question 10
q-89634.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\frac{3{x}^{2}}{\pi (1+{x}^{6})},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ),
$$

find the cumulative distribution function $F(x).$
q-89634.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a continuous random variable $X$ is the function $F(x)$ defined by

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}\frac{3{t}^{2}}{\pi (1+{t}^{6})}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\frac{\operatorname{arctan}⁡({t}^{3})}{\pi }|}_{-\infty }^{x} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})}{\pi }+\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

q-210782.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{33}(2+x),\, & 2\le x\le 5 \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

its cumulative distribution function is 

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<2 \\ h(x),\, & 2\le x\le 5 \\ 1,\, & x>5\end{aligned}
$$

where $h(x)=${{field-1}}.
q-210782.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $2\le x\le 5,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<2 \\ {\int }_{2}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t, & 2\le x\le 5 \\ 1, & x>5\end{aligned}
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{2}^{x}\frac{2}{33}(2+t)\,\text{d}t \\ \text{ } & ={(\frac{4}{33}t+\frac{{t}^{2}}{33})|}_{2}^{x} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{33}+\frac{4x}{33}-\frac{12}{33} \\  & =\frac{1}{33}({x}^{2}+4x-12) \\  & =\frac{1}{33}(x+6)(x-2).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<2 \\ \frac{1}{33}(x+6)(x-2), & 2\le x\le 5 \\ 1, & x>5.\end{aligned}
$$

q-89679.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}(4-x),\, & 2\le x\le 5 \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

its cumulative distribution function is 

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<2 \\ h(x),\, & 2\le x\le 5 \\ 1,\, & x>5.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the function $h(x).$
q-89679.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $2\le x\le 5,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<2 \\ {\int }_{2}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t, & 2\le x\le 5 \\ 1, & x>5\end{aligned}
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{2}^{x}\frac{2}{3}(4-t)\,\text{d}t \\ \text{ } & ={-\frac{1}{3}t(t-8)|}_{2}^{x} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}x(x-8)-4 \\  & =\frac{-{x}^{2}+8x-12}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<2 \\ \frac{-{x}^{2}+8x-12}{3}, & 2\le x\le 5 \\ 1, & x>5.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the random variable X has the probability density function f(x)={23(4−x),2≤x≤50,otherwise its cumulative distribution function is F(x)={0,x<2h(x),2≤x≤51,x>5. Find the function h(x).

a
−x2+4x−243
b
−x2+8x+12
c
−x2+8x−123
d
−x2−4x−33
e
−x2+4x−12
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since our random variable X has a probability distribution function f(x) that is strictly positive only for 2≤x≤5, the cumulative distribution function takes the following form: F(x)=P(X≤x)={0,x<2∫2xf(t)dt,2≤x≤51,x>5

For the given probability density function, we have ∫2xf(t)dt=∫2x23(4−t)dt =−13t(t−8)|2x=−13x(x−8)−4=−x2+8x−123.

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by F(x)={0,x<2−x2+8x−123,2≤x≤51,x>5.

q-89745.name: Question 13
q-89745.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1 \\ 1-\frac{1}{{x}^{6}}, & x\ge 1,\end{aligned}
$$

find $P(X\le 2).$
q-89745.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a continuous random variable $X$ is the function $F(x)$ defined by

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x).
$$

Hence, the required probability is $F(2)=1-\frac{1}{{2}^{6}}=\frac{63}{64}.$

q-126172.name: Question 14
q-126172.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0 \\ \frac{x}{2}, & 0\le x<2 \\ 1, & x\ge 2,\end{aligned}
$$

find $P(1\le X\le 3).$
q-126172.worked_solution:
Remember that for continuous random variables, it doesn't matter whether or not we include the endpoints of the interval. So we can perform the computation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1\le X\le 3) & =P(1<X\le 3) \\  & =P(X\le 3)-P(X\le 1) \\  & =F(3)-F(1) \\  & =1-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
